# Parser support types
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ParsedPort:
    """A ``hw.module``-style port declaration found in a signature."""

    __slots__ = ("name", "type", "direction")

    def __init__(self, name: str, type: Optional[Type], direction: str) -> None:
        self.name = name
        self.type = type
        self.direction = direction

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging helper
        return f"ParsedPort({self.direction} {self.name}: {self.type})"


class _ForwardRef(Value):
    """Placeholder for an SSA name used before its definition is parsed."""

    def __init__(self, name: str, line: int, col: int) -> None:
        super().__init__(IndexType(), name)
        self.line = line
        self.col = col

    def __repr__(self) -> str:  # pragma: no cover - debugging helper
        return f"_ForwardRef(%{self.name})"


class _Scope:
    """One SSA naming scope (a region)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.values: Dict[str, Value] = {}
        self.pending: Dict[str, _ForwardRef] = {}
        self.blocks: Dict[str, Block] = {}
        self.pending_blocks: Dict[str, Block] = {}


#: Ops that own graph regions where forward references are legal.
GRAPH_REGION_OPS = {"hw.module", "hw.module.extern", "firrtl.module", "fsm.machine"}

#: Operations whose signature declares ports rather than plain block arguments.
PORT_LIST_OPS = {"hw.module", "hw.module.extern", "firrtl.module", "fsm.machine"}

#: Keyword-valued attribute names, per operation.
KEYWORD_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES = {
    "arith.cmpi": "predicate",
    "arith.cmpf": "predicate",
    "comb.icmp": "predicate",
    "llhd.cmp": "predicate",
}


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Parser
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class Parser:
    """Recursive-descent parser producing the IR defined in :mod:`src.mlir.ir`."""

    def __init__(
        self,
        source: str,
        context: Optional[MLIRContext] = None,
        filename: Optional[str] = None,
    ) -> None:
        self.source = source
        self.context = context if context is not None else get_default_context()
        self.filename = filename
        self.tokens = Lexer(source).tokens
        self.pos = 0
        self._scopes: List[_Scope] = []

    # -- token helpers ----------------------------------------------------
    @property
    def current(self) -> Token:
        return self.tokens[self.pos]

    def peek(self, offset: int = 1) -> Token:
        index = min(self.pos + offset, len(self.tokens) - 1)
        return self.tokens[index]

    def advance(self) -> Token:
        token = self.tokens[self.pos]
        if token.kind is not TokenKind.EOF:
            self.pos += 1
        return token

    def check(self, kind: TokenKind, value: Optional[str] = None) -> bool:
        token = self.current
        if token.kind is not kind:
            return False
        return value is None or token.value == value

    def accept(self, kind: TokenKind, value: Optional[str] = None) -> Optional[Token]:
        if self.check(kind, value):
            return self.advance()
        return None

    def expect(self, kind: TokenKind, value: Optional[str] = None) -> Token:
        if not self.check(kind, value):
            expected = value if value is not None else kind.name
            raise ParseError(
                f"expected {expected} but found {self.current.value!r}",
                self.current.line,
                self.current.col,
            )
        return self.advance()

    def _loc(self, token: Optional[Token] = None) -> Location:
        token = token or self.current
        if self.filename is None:
            return Location(filename="<string>", line=token.line, column=token.col)
        return Location(filename=self.filename, line=token.line, column=token.col)

    # -- scope helpers ----------------------------------------------------
    def _push_scope(self) -> _Scope:
        scope = _Scope()
        self._scopes.append(scope)
        return scope

    def _pop_scope(self) -> _Scope:
        scope = self._scopes.pop()
        if scope.pending:
            name, ref = next(iter(scope.pending.items()))
            raise ParseError(f"use of undefined value '%{name}'", ref.line, ref.col)
        return scope

    def _define_value(self, name: str, value: Value) -> None:
        scope = self._scopes[-1]
        placeholder = scope.pending.pop(name, None)
        if placeholder is not None:
            placeholder.replace_all_uses_with(value)
        scope.values[name] = value

    def _lookup_value(self, name: str, token: Token) -> Value:
        for scope in reversed(self._scopes):
            if name in scope.values:
                return scope.values[name]
        # Not defined yet - create (or reuse) a forward reference in the
        # innermost scope.  Graph regions resolve these later in the block.
        scope = self._scopes[-1]
        existing = scope.pending.get(name)
        if existing is not None:
            return existing
        placeholder = _ForwardRef(name, token.line, token.col)
        scope.pending[name] = placeholder
        return placeholder

    def _lookup_block(self, label: str) -> Block:
        scope = self._scopes[-1]
        block = scope.blocks.get(label) or scope.pending_blocks.get(label)
        if block is None:
            block = Block(label=label)
            scope.pending_blocks[label] = block
        return block

    def _define_block(self, label: str) -> Block:
        scope = self._scopes[-1]
        block = scope.pending_blocks.pop(label, None)
        if block is None:
            block = Block(label=label)
        block.label = label
        scope.blocks[label] = block
        return block

    # -- entry points -----------------------------------------------------
    def parse_module(self) -> ModuleOp:
        """Parse a whole file.

        A top-level ``module { ... }`` is used as-is; a bare sequence of
        operations is wrapped in an implicit module, exactly like ``mlir-opt``.
        """
        if self.check(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER, "module") or self.check(
            TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER, "builtin.module"
        ):
            op = self._parse_operation()
            if isinstance(op, ModuleOp):
                self._finish(op)
                return op
            module = ModuleOp(context=self.context)
            module.block.append(op)
            self._finish(module)
            return module

        module = ModuleOp(context=self.context)
        self._push_scope()
        while not self.check(TokenKind.EOF):
            module.block.append(self._parse_operation())
        self._pop_scope()
        self._finish(module)
        return module

    def _finish(self, module: ModuleOp) -> None:
        if not self.check(TokenKind.EOF):
            raise ParseError(
                f"unexpected trailing token {self.current.value!r}",
                self.current.line,
                self.current.col,
            )

    # -- operations -------------------------------------------------------
    def _parse_operation(self) -> Operation:
        start = self.current
        result_names = self._parse_result_names()

        name_token = self.current
        op_name = self._parse_operation_name()
        generic_form = name_token.kind is TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL

        operands: List[Value] = []
        successors: List[Block] = []
        attributes: Dict[str, Attribute] = {}
        regions: List[Region] = []
        ports: List[ParsedPort] = []
        keywords: List[str] = []
        signature: Optional[FunctionType] = None
        arg_names: List[Optional[str]] = []
        arg_types: List[Type] = []

        symbol: Optional[str] = None
        while self.check(TokenKind.SYMBOL_IDENTIFIER):
            token = self.advance()
            if symbol is None:
                symbol = token.value
                attributes.setdefault("sym_name", StringAttr(token.value))
            else:
                attributes.setdefault("callee", FlatSymbolRefAttr(token.value))
        if symbol is not None and op_name in ("func.call", "std.call"):
            attributes.pop("sym_name", None)
            attributes["callee"] = FlatSymbolRefAttr(symbol)

        # Signature / operand parenthesis group -------------------------
        signature_entries: List[ParsedPort] = []
        has_directions = False
        if self.check(TokenKind.LPAREN):
            group = self._parse_paren_group()
            signature_entries = group["entries"]
            has_directions = group["has_directions"]
            operands.extend(group["operands"])

        # Trailing keywords / operands / successors ----------------------
        while True:
            if self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER):
                if self._ssa_starts_new_statement():
                    break
                token = self.advance()
                operands.append(self._lookup_value(token.value, token))
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.CARET_IDENTIFIER):
                if self._caret_is_label_definition():
                    break
                token = self.advance()
                successors.append(self._lookup_block(token.value))
                if self.check(TokenKind.LPAREN):
                    group = self._parse_paren_group()
                    operands.extend(group["operands"])
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.SYMBOL_IDENTIFIER):
                token = self.advance()
                attributes.setdefault("callee", FlatSymbolRefAttr(token.value))
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.INTEGER_LITERAL) or self.check(TokenKind.FLOAT_LITERAL):
                token = self.advance()
                attributes.setdefault("value", self._literal_attribute(token))
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL):
                token = self.advance()
                attributes.setdefault("value", StringAttr(token.value))
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER):
                # A bare word here is a custom-assembly keyword such as the
                # ``sgt`` of ``arith.cmpi`` or the ``reset`` of ``seq.compreg``.
                if self._bare_identifier_starts_new_statement():
                    break
                token = self.advance()
                keywords.append(token.value)
                continue
            if self.check(TokenKind.LBRACKET):
                attributes.setdefault("operand_segment_sizes", self._parse_array_attribute())
                continue
            break

        # Attribute dictionary ------------------------------------------
        if self._at_attribute_dictionary():
            attributes.update(self._parse_attribute_dictionary())
        if self.accept(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER, "attributes"):
            if self._at_attribute_dictionary():
                attributes.update(self._parse_attribute_dictionary())

        # Region --------------------------------------------------------
        trailing_types: List[Type] = []
        if self.check(TokenKind.ARROW):
            self.advance()
            trailing_types = self._parse_type_list_or_single()

        if self.check(TokenKind.COLON):
            self.advance()
            colon_types = self._parse_type_list_or_single()
            if colon_types and isinstance(colon_types[0], FunctionType) and len(colon_types) == 1:
                signature = colon_types[0]
                trailing_types = list(signature.results)
            else:
                trailing_types = colon_types

        if self.check(TokenKind.ARROW):
            self.advance()
            trailing_types = self._parse_type_list_or_single()

        # Build the operation -------------------------------------------
        canonical = _dialects.canonical_op_name(op_name, self.context)
        op_class = _dialects.resolve_op_class(op_name, self.context) or Operation

        if canonical in KEYWORD_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES and keywords:
            attributes.setdefault(
                KEYWORD_ATTRIBUTE_NAMES[canonical], StringAttr(keywords[0])
            )
        if keywords:
            attributes.setdefault("assembly_keywords",
                                  ArrayAttr([StringAttr(k) for k in keywords]))

        result_types = op_class.result_types_from_trailing(
            trailing_types, len(result_names)
        )

        # Ports / function signature -------------------------------------
        if signature_entries and (has_directions or canonical in PORT_LIST_OPS):
            ports = signature_entries
            input_types = [p.type for p in ports if p.direction in ("in", "inout")]
            output_types = [p.type for p in ports if p.direction == "out"]
            signature = FunctionType(
                [t for t in input_types if t is not None],
                [t for t in output_types if t is not None],
            )
            attributes.setdefault("function_type", TypeAttr(signature))
            attributes.setdefault(
                "port_names", ArrayAttr([StringAttr(p.name) for p in ports])
            )
            attributes.setdefault(
                "port_directions", ArrayAttr([StringAttr(p.direction) for p in ports])
            )
            arg_names = [p.name for p in ports if p.direction in ("in", "inout")]
            arg_types = [t for t in input_types if t is not None]
        elif signature_entries or canonical in ("func.func", "builtin.func"):
            arg_names = [p.name or None for p in signature_entries]
            arg_types = [p.type for p in signature_entries if p.type is not None]
            signature = FunctionType(arg_types, trailing_types)
            attributes.setdefault("function_type", TypeAttr(signature))

        has_region = self._at_region_start()
        op = op_class.build_parsed(
            name=canonical,
            operands=operands,
            result_types=result_types,
            attributes=attributes,
            successors=successors,
            regions=None,
            location=self._loc(start),
            result_names=result_names,
        )

        if has_region:
            region = self._parse_region(
                arg_types=arg_types,
                arg_names=arg_names,
                graph_region=canonical in GRAPH_REGION_OPS,
            )
            op.add_region(region)

        # Optional trailing ``loc(...)``.
        if self.check(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER, "loc"):
            self.advance()
            self._skip_balanced(TokenKind.LPAREN, TokenKind.RPAREN)

        for index, res_name in enumerate(result_names):
            if res_name is None or index >= op.num_results:
                continue
            self._define_value(res_name, op.result(index))

        return op

    # -- pieces -----------------------------------------------------------
    def _parse_result_names(self) -> List[Optional[str]]:
        """Parse ``%a, %b =`` returning the SSA names (empty when absent)."""
        if not self._ssa_starts_new_statement():
            return []
        names: List[Optional[str]] = []
        while True:
            token = self.expect(TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER)
            names.append(token.value)
            if self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                continue
            break
        self.expect(TokenKind.EQUAL)
        return names

    def _ssa_starts_new_statement(self) -> bool:
        """Is the SSA name at the cursor the start of a ``%a, %b =`` result list?"""
        if not self.check(TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER):
            return False
        offset = 0
        while True:
            token = self.peek(offset)
            if token.kind is not TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER:
                return False
            offset += 1
            nxt = self.peek(offset)
            if nxt.kind is TokenKind.COMMA:
                offset += 1
                continue
            return nxt.kind is TokenKind.EQUAL

    def _caret_is_label_definition(self) -> bool:
        """Is ``^bbN`` at the cursor a block label rather than a successor?

        A label definition is followed by ``:`` - possibly after a parenthesised
        argument list, as in ``^bb1(%x: i32):``.
        """
        if not self.check(TokenKind.CARET_IDENTIFIER):
            return False
        offset = 1
        if self.peek(offset).kind is TokenKind.LPAREN:
            depth = 0
            while True:
                kind = self.peek(offset).kind
                if kind is TokenKind.LPAREN:
                    depth += 1
                elif kind is TokenKind.RPAREN:
                    depth -= 1
                    if depth == 0:
                        offset += 1
                        break
                elif kind is TokenKind.EOF:
                    return False
                offset += 1
        return self.peek(offset).kind is TokenKind.COLON

    def _parse_operation_name(self) -> str:
        if self.check(TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL):
            return self.advance().value
        token = self.expect(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER)
        return token.value

    def _bare_identifier_starts_new_statement(self) -> bool:
        """Heuristic: is this bare word the start of the *next* operation?

        Custom assembly keywords (``eq``, ``sgt``, ``reset``) never name a
        registered operation, whereas a new statement always begins with one -
        either dotted (``comb.add``) or a registered bare alias (``return``,
        ``br``, ``module``).
        """
        token = self.current
        if "." in token.value:
            return True
        return _dialects.resolve_op_class(token.value, self.context) is not None

    def _parse_paren_group(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Parse ``( ... )`` after an op name.

        The group is either a port/argument signature (entries carry a type) or
        a plain operand list (entries are bare SSA names).  ``in``/``out``/
        ``inout`` keywords mark it as a hardware-style port list.
        """
        self.expect(TokenKind.LPAREN)
        entries: List[ParsedPort] = []
        operands: List[Value] = []
        has_directions = False

        while not self.check(TokenKind.RPAREN):
            direction = "in"
            if self.check(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER) and self.current.value in (
                "in",
                "out",
                "inout",
            ):
                direction = self.advance().value
                has_directions = True

            if self.check(TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER):
                token = self.advance()
                if self.check(TokenKind.COLON):
                    self.advance()
                    entries.append(ParsedPort(token.value, self._parse_type(), direction))
                else:
                    operands.append(self._lookup_value(token.value, token))
            elif self.check(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER) and self.peek().kind is TokenKind.COLON:
                entry_name = self.advance().value
                self.expect(TokenKind.COLON)
                entries.append(ParsedPort(entry_name, self._parse_type(), direction))
            else:
                entries.append(ParsedPort("", self._parse_type(), direction))

            if not self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                break

        self.expect(TokenKind.RPAREN)
        return {
            "entries": entries,
            "operands": operands,
            "has_directions": has_directions,
        }

    def _at_region_start(self) -> bool:
        return self.check(TokenKind.LBRACE) and not self._at_attribute_dictionary()

    def _at_attribute_dictionary(self) -> bool:
        if not self.check(TokenKind.LBRACE):
            return False
        nxt = self.peek()
        if nxt.kind is TokenKind.RBRACE:
            return True
        if nxt.kind in (TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER, TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL):
            return self.peek(2).kind is TokenKind.EQUAL
        return False

    def _parse_attribute_dictionary(self) -> Dict[str, Attribute]:
        self.expect(TokenKind.LBRACE)
        attributes: Dict[str, Attribute] = {}
        while not self.check(TokenKind.RBRACE):
            if self.check(TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL):
                key = self.advance().value
            else:
                key = self.expect(TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER).value
            if self.accept(TokenKind.EQUAL):
                attributes[key] = self._parse_attribute_value()
            else:
                attributes[key] = UnitAttr()
            if not self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                break
        self.expect(TokenKind.RBRACE)
        return attributes

    def _literal_attribute(self, token: Token) -> Attribute:
        if token.kind is TokenKind.FLOAT_LITERAL:
            return FloatAttr(float(token.value))
        base = 16 if token.value.lower().startswith(("0x", "-0x")) else 10
        return IntegerAttr(int(token.value, base))

    def _parse_array_attribute(self) -> ArrayAttr:
        self.expect(TokenKind.LBRACKET)
        elements: List[Attribute] = []
        while not self.check(TokenKind.RBRACKET):
            elements.append(self._parse_attribute_value())
            if not self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                break
        self.expect(TokenKind.RBRACKET)
        return ArrayAttr(elements)

    def _parse_attribute_value(self) -> Attribute:
        token = self.current
        if token.kind is TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL:
            self.advance()
            return StringAttr(token.value)
        if token.kind in (TokenKind.INTEGER_LITERAL, TokenKind.FLOAT_LITERAL):
            self.advance()
            attr = self._literal_attribute(token)
            if self.accept(TokenKind.COLON):
                attr_type = self._parse_type()
                if isinstance(attr, IntegerAttr):
                    return IntegerAttr(attr.value, attr_type)
                return FloatAttr(attr.value, attr_type)
            return attr
        if token.kind is TokenKind.SYMBOL_IDENTIFIER:
            self.advance()
            return FlatSymbolRefAttr(token.value)
        if token.kind is TokenKind.LBRACKET:
            return self._parse_array_attribute()
        if token.kind is TokenKind.LBRACE:
            return DictAttr(self._parse_attribute_dictionary())
        if token.kind is TokenKind.TYPE_IDENTIFIER:
            return TypeAttr(self._parse_type())
        if token.kind is TokenKind.ATTRIBUTE_ALIAS:
            self.advance()
            return StringAttr(f"#{token.value}")
        if token.kind is TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER:
            if token.value in ("true", "false"):
                self.advance()
                return BoolAttr(token.value == "true")
            if token.value == "unit":
                self.advance()
                return UnitAttr()
            if token.value == "dense":
                self.advance()
                self._skip_balanced(TokenKind.LANGLE, TokenKind.RANGLE)
                if self.accept(TokenKind.COLON):
                    return TypeAttr(self._parse_type())
                return UnitAttr()
            # A type used as an attribute, e.g. ``function_type = (i32) -> i32``.
            return TypeAttr(self._parse_type())
        if token.kind is TokenKind.LPAREN:
            return TypeAttr(self._parse_type())
        raise ParseError(
            f"unexpected attribute value {token.value!r}", token.line, token.col
        )

    def _skip_balanced(self, open_kind: TokenKind, close_kind: TokenKind) -> None:
        self.expect(open_kind)
        depth = 1
        while depth and not self.check(TokenKind.EOF):
            if self.check(open_kind):
                depth += 1
            elif self.check(close_kind):
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    self.advance()
                    return
            self.advance()

    # -- regions / blocks -------------------------------------------------
    def _parse_region(
        self,
        arg_types: Optional[Sequence[Type]] = None,
        arg_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
        graph_region: bool = False,
    ) -> Region:
        self.expect(TokenKind.LBRACE)
        region = Region()
        scope = self._push_scope()

        entry = Block(arg_types=list(arg_types or ()), arg_names=list(arg_names or ()))
        for arg in entry.arguments:
            if arg.name:
                scope.values[arg.name] = arg
        region.add_block(entry)
        current = entry

        while not self.check(TokenKind.RBRACE) and not self.check(TokenKind.EOF):
            if self.check(TokenKind.CARET_IDENTIFIER):
                label_token = self.advance()
                block = self._define_block(label_token.value)
                block_arg_types: List[Type] = []
                block_arg_names: List[Optional[str]] = []
                if self.check(TokenKind.LPAREN):
                    self.advance()
                    while not self.check(TokenKind.RPAREN):
                        arg_token = self.expect(TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER)
                        self.expect(TokenKind.COLON)
                        block_arg_types.append(self._parse_type())
                        block_arg_names.append(arg_token.value)
                        if not self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                            break
                    self.expect(TokenKind.RPAREN)
                self.expect(TokenKind.COLON)
                for atype, aname in zip(block_arg_types, block_arg_names):
                    arg = block.add_argument(atype, aname)
                    if aname:
                        scope.values[aname] = arg
                if block.parent is None:
                    region.add_block(block)
                current = block
                continue
            current.append(self._parse_operation())

        self.expect(TokenKind.RBRACE)

        # Blocks referenced by a branch but never defined are an error.
        if scope.pending_blocks:
            label = next(iter(scope.pending_blocks))
            raise ParseError(f"reference to undefined block '^{label}'")
        if graph_region:
            # Graph regions may close over values defined later in the same
            # region; the placeholders were patched as definitions appeared.
            if scope.pending:
                name, ref = next(iter(scope.pending.items()))
                raise ParseError(f"use of undefined value '%{name}'", ref.line, ref.col)
            self._scopes.pop()
        else:
            self._pop_scope()
        return region

    # -- types ------------------------------------------------------------
    def _parse_type_list_or_single(self) -> List[Type]:
        if self.check(TokenKind.LPAREN):
            saved = self.pos
            types = self._parse_paren_type_list()
            if self.check(TokenKind.ARROW):
                self.advance()
                results = self._parse_type_list_or_single()
                return [FunctionType(types, results)]
            self.pos = saved
            return self._parse_paren_type_list()
        types = [self._parse_type()]
        while self.check(TokenKind.COMMA):
            self.advance()
            types.append(self._parse_type())
        if self.check(TokenKind.ARROW):
            self.advance()
            results = self._parse_type_list_or_single()
            return [FunctionType(types, results)]
        return types

    def _parse_paren_type_list(self) -> List[Type]:
        self.expect(TokenKind.LPAREN)
        types: List[Type] = []
        while not self.check(TokenKind.RPAREN):
            types.append(self._parse_type())
            if not self.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                break
        self.expect(TokenKind.RPAREN)
        return types

    def _parse_type(self) -> Type:
        token = self.current
        if token.kind is TokenKind.TYPE_IDENTIFIER:
            self.advance()
            dialect, _, mnemonic = token.value.partition(".")
            data = ""
            if self.check(TokenKind.LANGLE):
                data = self._capture_balanced(TokenKind.LANGLE, TokenKind.RANGLE)
            return OpaqueType(dialect, mnemonic or dialect, data)
        if token.kind is TokenKind.LPAREN:
            inputs = self._parse_paren_type_list()
            if self.accept(TokenKind.ARROW):
                results = self._parse_type_list_or_single()
                return FunctionType(inputs, results)
            return TupleType(inputs)
        if token.kind is TokenKind.BARE_IDENTIFIER:
            name = token.value
            if name == "index":
                self.advance()
                return IndexType()
            if name == "none":
                self.advance()
                return NoneType_()
            if name == "tuple":
                self.advance()
                body = self._capture_balanced(TokenKind.LANGLE, TokenKind.RANGLE)
                inner = Parser(body, self.context)
                inner._push_scope()
                types = [inner._parse_type()]
                while inner.accept(TokenKind.COMMA):
                    types.append(inner._parse_type())
                return TupleType(types)
            if name in ("memref", "tensor", "vector"):
                self.advance()
                data = self._capture_balanced(TokenKind.LANGLE, TokenKind.RANGLE)
                return OpaqueType("builtin", name, data)
            integer = _parse_integer_type_name(name)
            if integer is not None:
                self.advance()
                return integer
            float_type = _parse_float_type_name(name)
            if float_type is not None:
                self.advance()
                return float_type
            self.advance()
            return OpaqueType("", name)
        raise ParseError(f"expected a type but found {token.value!r}", token.line, token.col)

    def _capture_balanced(self, open_kind: TokenKind, close_kind: TokenKind) -> str:
        self.expect(open_kind)
        depth = 1
        pieces: List[str] = []
        while depth and not self.check(TokenKind.EOF):
            if self.check(open_kind):
                depth += 1
            elif self.check(close_kind):
                depth -= 1
                if depth == 0:
                    self.advance()
                    break
            token = self.advance()
            if token.kind is TokenKind.TYPE_IDENTIFIER:
                pieces.append("!" + token.value)
            elif token.kind is TokenKind.SSA_IDENTIFIER:
                pieces.append("%" + token.value)
            elif token.kind is TokenKind.STRING_LITERAL:
                pieces.append(f'"{token.value}"')
            else:
                pieces.append(token.value)
        return "".join(pieces)


def _parse_integer_type_name(name: str) -> Optional[IntegerType]:
    for prefix, signedness in (("si", "signed"), ("ui", "unsigned"), ("i", "signless")):
        if name.startswith(prefix) and name[len(prefix):].isdigit():
            return IntegerType(int(name[len(prefix):]), signedness)
    return None


def _parse_float_type_name(name: str) -> Optional[FloatType]:
    if name == "bf16":
        return FloatType(16, "bf16")
    if name.startswith("f") and name[1:].isdigit():
        return FloatType(int(name[1:]))
    return None


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Module-level helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


def parse(source: str, context: Optional[MLIRContext] = None,
          filename: Optional[str] = None) -> ModuleOp:
    """Parse MLIR text into a :class:`~src.mlir.ir.ModuleOp`."""
    return Parser(source, context, filename).parse_module()


def parse_file(path: str, context: Optional[MLIRContext] = None) -> ModuleOp:
    with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        return parse(handle.read(), context, filename=path)

"""Dialect registry.

Importing this package registers the ``builtin``, ``func``, ``arith`` and ``cf``
dialects with the default :class:`~src.mlir.ir.MLIRContext`.  The CIRCT layer
adds ``hw``/``comb``/``seq`` to the same context, which is how the shared parser
learns to read hardware IR.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Dict, Optional

from ..ir import MLIRContext, Operation, get_default_context
from . import arith as arith
from . import builtin as builtin
from . import cf as cf
from . import func as func

#: Alternate op spellings accepted by the parser (bare ``return``, ``br``, ...).
OP_ALIASES: Dict[str, type] = {"module": builtin.ModuleOp}
OP_ALIASES.update(func.LEGACY_OP_ALIASES)
OP_ALIASES.update(cf.LEGACY_OP_ALIASES)


def register_alias(spelling: str, op_class: type) -> None:
    """Teach the parser that ``spelling`` maps onto ``op_class``."""
    OP_ALIASES[spelling] = op_class


def resolve_op_class(
    name: str, context: Optional[MLIRContext] = None
) -> Optional[type]:
    """Look up the :class:`Operation` subclass registered for ``name``."""
    ctx = context if context is not None else get_default_context()
    op_class = ctx.lookup_operation(name)
    if op_class is not None:
        return op_class
    return OP_ALIASES.get(name)


def canonical_op_name(name: str, context: Optional[MLIRContext] = None) -> str:
    """Normalise legacy spellings (``return`` -> ``func.return``)."""
    op_class = resolve_op_class(name, context)
    if op_class is None:
        return name
    canonical = op_class.operation_name()
    return canonical or name


__all__ = [
    "arith",
    "builtin",
    "cf",
    "func",
    "OP_ALIASES",
    "register_alias",
    "resolve_op_class",
    "canonical_op_name",
]

2	
3	Every operation here implements :meth:`Operation.fold`, which is what the greedy
4	constant-folding driver in :mod:`src.mlir.pattern` relies on.
5	"""
6	from __future__ import annotations
7	
8	from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence

11	    Attribute,
12	    Dialect,
13	    IntegerAttr,
14	    IntegerType,
15	    Location,
16	    Operation,

22	)

24	ARITH_DIALECT = Dialect("arith", get_default_context())
25

27	def _wrap(value: int, type: Optional[Type]) -> int:
28	    """Truncate ``value`` to the bitwidth of ``type`` using two's complement."""
29	    width = type.bitwidth() if type is not None else None
30	    if not width:
31	        return value
32	    mask = (1 << width) - 1
33	    value &= mask
34	    # Signless integers are printed as signed in MLIR's arith dialect.
35	    if width > 1 and value >= (1 << (width - 1)):
36	        value -= 1 << width
37	    return value

40	class ConstantOp(Operation):
41	    """``arith.constant 42 : i32``."""
42	
43	    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.constant"
44	    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE, Trait.CONSTANT_LIKE)
45	
46	    def __init__(
47	        self,
48	        value: Optional[int] = None,
49	        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
50	        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
51	        location: Optional[Location] = None,
52	        name: Optional[str] = None,
53	        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
54	    ) -> None:
55	        attrs: Dict[str, Attribute] = dict(attributes or {})
56	        rtype = result_type if result_type is not None else IntegerType(32)
57	        if value is not None:
58	            attrs["value"] = IntegerAttr(value, rtype)
59	        super().__init__(
60	            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
61	            result_types=[rtype],
62	            attributes=attrs,
63	            location=location,
64	            result_names=result_names,
65	        )

68	    def value(self) -> Optional[int]:
69	        attr = self.attributes.get("value")
70	        if attr is None:
71	            return None
72	        raw = attr.value
73	        return raw if isinstance(raw, int) else None

75	    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:
76	        value = self.value
77	        return None if value is None else [value]

80	class BinaryArithOp(Operation):
81	    """Shared base for two-operand, single-result integer operations."""
82	
83	    OPERATION_NAME: Optional[str] = None
84	    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE, Trait.SAME_OPERANDS_AND_RESULT_TYPE)
85	
86	    #: ``(lhs, rhs) -> int``
87	    EVALUATOR: Optional[Callable[[int, int], int]] = None
88	
89	    def __init__(
90	        self,
91	        operands: Optional[Sequence[Value]] = None,
92	        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
93	        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
94	        location: Optional[Location] = None,
95	        name: Optional[str] = None,
96	        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
97	    ) -> None:
98	        ops = list(operands or ())
99	        rtype = result_type
100	        if rtype is None and ops:
101	            rtype = ops[0].type
102	        super().__init__(
103	            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
104	            operands=ops,
105	            result_types=[rtype] if rtype is not None else [],
106	            attributes=attributes,
107	            location=location,
108	            result_names=result_names,
109	        )
110	
111	    # -- folding ----------------------------------------------------------
112	    def constant_operands(self) -> Optional[List[int]]:
113	        """Return the operand constants, or ``None`` if any is non-constant."""
114	        values: List[int] = []
115	        for operand in self.operands:
116	            defining = operand.defining_op
117	            if defining is None or not defining.is_constant_like:
118	                return None
119	            folded = defining.fold()
120	            if not folded or not isinstance(folded[0], int):
121	                return None
122	            values.append(folded[0])
123	        return values
124	
125	    def evaluate(self, lhs: int, rhs: int) -> int:
126	        evaluator = type(self).EVALUATOR
127	        if evaluator is None:
128	            raise NotImplementedError(f"{self.name} has no evaluator")
129	        return evaluator(lhs, rhs)
130	
131	    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:
132	        constants = self.constant_operands()
133	        if constants is None or len(constants) != 2:
134	            return None
135	        try:
136	            raw = self.evaluate(constants[0], constants[1])
137	        except (ZeroDivisionError, NotImplementedError):
138	            return None
139	        rtype = self.result_types[0] if self.result_types else None
140	        return [_wrap(raw, rtype)]

272	        cls, trailing_types: Sequence[Type], num_results: int
273	    ) -> List[Type]:
274	        # ``arith.cmpi sgt, %a, %b : i32`` - the trailing type is the operand
275	        # type; the result is always a single ``i1``.
276	        return [IntegerType(1)] * num_results

278	    def verify_op(self) -> List[str]:
279	        predicate = self.predicate
280	        if predicate is not None and predicate not in CMPI_PREDICATES:
281	            return [f"'arith.cmpi' has unknown predicate {predicate!r}"]

284	    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:

286	        if predicate not in CMPI_PREDICATES:

288	        constants: List[int] = []
289	        for operand in self.operands:

292	                return None
293	            folded = defining.fold()
294	            if not folded or not isinstance(folded[0], int):
295	                return None
296	            constants.append(folded[0])

"""The ``arith`` dialect: integer constants, arithmetic, bitwise ops, comparisons.

Every operation here implements :meth:`Operation.fold`, which is what the greedy
constant-folding driver in :mod:`src.mlir.pattern` relies on.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Callable, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence

from ..ir import (
    Attribute,
    Dialect,
    IntegerAttr,
    IntegerType,
    Location,
    Operation,
    StringAttr,
    Trait,
    Type,
    Value,
    get_default_context,
)

ARITH_DIALECT = Dialect("arith", get_default_context())


def _wrap(value: int, type: Optional[Type]) -> int:
    """Truncate ``value`` to the bitwidth of ``type`` using two's complement."""
    width = type.bitwidth() if type is not None else None
    if not width:
        return value
    mask = (1 << width) - 1
    value &= mask
    # Signless integers are printed as signed in MLIR's arith dialect.
    if width > 1 and value >= (1 << (width - 1)):
        value -= 1 << width
    return value


class ConstantOp(Operation):
    """``arith.constant 42 : i32``."""

    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.constant"
    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE, Trait.CONSTANT_LIKE)

    def __init__(
        self,
        value: Optional[int] = None,
        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
        location: Optional[Location] = None,
        name: Optional[str] = None,
        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        attrs: Dict[str, Attribute] = dict(attributes or {})
        rtype = result_type if result_type is not None else IntegerType(32)
        if value is not None:
            attrs["value"] = IntegerAttr(value, rtype)
        super().__init__(
            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
            result_types=[rtype],
            attributes=attrs,
            location=location,
            result_names=result_names,
        )

    @property
    def value(self) -> Optional[int]:
        attr = self.attributes.get("value")
        if attr is None:
            return None
        raw = attr.value
        return raw if isinstance(raw, int) else None

    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:
        value = self.value
        return None if value is None else [value]


class BinaryArithOp(Operation):
    """Shared base for two-operand, single-result integer operations."""

    OPERATION_NAME: Optional[str] = None
    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE, Trait.SAME_OPERANDS_AND_RESULT_TYPE)

    #: ``(lhs, rhs) -> int``
    EVALUATOR: Optional[Callable[[int, int], int]] = None

    def __init__(
        self,
        operands: Optional[Sequence[Value]] = None,
        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
        location: Optional[Location] = None,
        name: Optional[str] = None,
        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        ops = list(operands or ())
        rtype = result_type
        if rtype is None and ops:
            rtype = ops[0].type
        super().__init__(
            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
            operands=ops,
            result_types=[rtype] if rtype is not None else [],
            attributes=attributes,
            location=location,
            result_names=result_names,
        )

    # -- folding ----------------------------------------------------------
    def constant_operands(self) -> Optional[List[int]]:
        """Return the operand constants, or ``None`` if any is non-constant."""
        values: List[int] = []
        for operand in self.operands:
            defining = operand.defining_op
            if defining is None or not defining.is_constant_like:
                return None
            folded = defining.fold()
            if not folded or not isinstance(folded[0], int):
                return None
            values.append(folded[0])
        return values

    def evaluate(self, lhs: int, rhs: int) -> int:
        evaluator = type(self).EVALUATOR
        if evaluator is None:
            raise NotImplementedError(f"{self.name} has no evaluator")
        return evaluator(lhs, rhs)

    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:
        constants = self.constant_operands()
        if constants is None or len(constants) != 2:
            return None
        try:
            raw = self.evaluate(constants[0], constants[1])
        except (ZeroDivisionError, NotImplementedError):
            return None
        rtype = self.result_types[0] if self.result_types else None
        return [_wrap(raw, rtype)]


class AddIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.addi"
    TRAITS = BinaryArithOp.TRAITS + (Trait.COMMUTATIVE,)
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a + b)


class SubIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.subi"
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a - b)


class MulIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.muli"
    TRAITS = BinaryArithOp.TRAITS + (Trait.COMMUTATIVE,)
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a * b)


class DivSIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.divsi"

    def evaluate(self, lhs: int, rhs: int) -> int:
        if rhs == 0:
            raise ZeroDivisionError("arith.divsi by zero")
        quotient = abs(lhs) // abs(rhs)
        return quotient if (lhs < 0) == (rhs < 0) else -quotient


class DivUIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.divui"

    def evaluate(self, lhs: int, rhs: int) -> int:
        if rhs == 0:
            raise ZeroDivisionError("arith.divui by zero")
        return lhs // rhs


class RemSIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.remsi"

    def evaluate(self, lhs: int, rhs: int) -> int:
        if rhs == 0:
            raise ZeroDivisionError("arith.remsi by zero")
        remainder = abs(lhs) % abs(rhs)
        return remainder if lhs >= 0 else -remainder


class AndIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.andi"
    TRAITS = BinaryArithOp.TRAITS + (Trait.COMMUTATIVE, Trait.IDEMPOTENT)
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a & b)


class OrIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.ori"
    TRAITS = BinaryArithOp.TRAITS + (Trait.COMMUTATIVE, Trait.IDEMPOTENT)
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a | b)


class XOrIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.xori"
    TRAITS = BinaryArithOp.TRAITS + (Trait.COMMUTATIVE,)
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a ^ b)


class ShLIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.shli"
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a << b)


class ShRUIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.shrui"
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a >> b)


class ShRSIOp(BinaryArithOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.shrsi"
    EVALUATOR = staticmethod(lambda a, b: a >> b)


#: ``arith.cmpi`` predicates, in MLIR's declaration order.
CMPI_PREDICATES: Dict[str, Callable[[int, int], bool]] = {
    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "slt": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "sle": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "sgt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "sge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
    "ult": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "ule": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "ugt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "uge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


class CmpIOp(Operation):
    """``arith.cmpi sgt, %a, %b : i32`` producing an ``i1``."""

    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.cmpi"
    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE,)

    def __init__(
        self,
        predicate: Optional[str] = None,
        operands: Optional[Sequence[Value]] = None,
        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
        location: Optional[Location] = None,
        name: Optional[str] = None,
        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
    ) -> None:
        attrs: Dict[str, Attribute] = dict(attributes or {})
        if predicate is not None:
            attrs["predicate"] = StringAttr(predicate)
        super().__init__(
            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
            operands=operands,
            result_types=[result_type or IntegerType(1)],
            attributes=attrs,
            location=location,
            result_names=result_names,
        )

    @property
    def predicate(self) -> Optional[str]:
        attr = self.attributes.get("predicate")
        return attr.value if attr is not None else None

    @classmethod
    def result_types_from_trailing(
        cls, trailing_types: Sequence[Type], num_results: int
    ) -> List[Type]:
        # ``arith.cmpi sgt, %a, %b : i32`` - the trailing type is the operand
        # type; the result is always a single ``i1``.
        return [IntegerType(1)] * num_results

    def verify_op(self) -> List[str]:
        predicate = self.predicate
        if predicate is not None and predicate not in CMPI_PREDICATES:
            return [f"'arith.cmpi' has unknown predicate {predicate!r}"]
        return []

    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:
        predicate = self.predicate
        if predicate not in CMPI_PREDICATES:
            return None
        constants: List[int] = []
        for operand in self.operands:
            defining = operand.defining_op
            if defining is None or not defining.is_constant_like:
                return None
            folded = defining.fold()
            if not folded or not isinstance(folded[0], int):
                return None
            constants.append(folded[0])
        if len(constants) != 2:
            return None
        return [1 if CMPI_PREDICATES[predicate](constants[0], constants[1]) else 0]


class SelectOp(Operation):
    """``arith.select %cond, %a, %b : i32``."""

    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.select"
    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE,)

    def __init__(
        self,
        operands: Optional[Sequence[Value]] = None,
        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
        location: Optional[Location] = None,
        name: Optional[str] = None,
        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        ops = list(operands or ())
        rtype = result_type
        if rtype is None and len(ops) >= 2:
            rtype = ops[1].type
        super().__init__(
            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
            operands=ops,
            result_types=[rtype] if rtype is not None else [],
            location=location,
            result_names=result_names,
        )


class ExtSIOp(Operation):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.extsi"
    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE,)

    def __init__(
        self,
        operands: Optional[Sequence[Value]] = None,
        result_type: Optional[Type] = None,
        location: Optional[Location] = None,
        name: Optional[str] = None,
        result_names: Optional[Sequence[Optional[str]]] = None,
    ) -> None:
        super().__init__(
            name=name or self.OPERATION_NAME,
            operands=operands,
            result_types=[result_type] if result_type is not None else [],
            location=location,
            result_names=result_names,
        )


class TruncIOp(ExtSIOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.trunci"


class ExtUIOp(ExtSIOp):
    OPERATION_NAME = "arith.extui"


#: Maps ``arith`` op names onto their classes so the parser can specialise.
ARITH_OPS: Dict[str, type] = {}
for _cls in (
    ConstantOp,
    AddIOp,
    SubIOp,
    MulIOp,
    DivSIOp,
    DivUIOp,
    RemSIOp,
    AndIOp,
    OrIOp,
    XOrIOp,
    ShLIOp,
    ShRUIOp,
    ShRSIOp,
    CmpIOp,
    SelectOp,
    ExtSIOp,
    ExtUIOp,
    TruncIOp,
):
    ARITH_DIALECT.register_operation(_cls)
    ARITH_OPS[_cls.OPERATION_NAME] = _cls
del _cls

__all__ = [
    "ARITH_DIALECT",
    "ARITH_OPS",
    "CMPI_PREDICATES",
    "ConstantOp",
    "BinaryArithOp",
    "AddIOp",
    "SubIOp",
    "MulIOp",
    "DivSIOp",
    "DivUIOp",
    "RemSIOp",
    "AndIOp",
    "OrIOp",
    "XOrIOp",
    "ShLIOp",
    "ShRUIOp",
    "ShRSIOp",
    "CmpIOp",
    "SelectOp",
    "ExtSIOp",
    "ExtUIOp",
    "TruncIOp",
]

1	"""The CIRCT ``hw`` dialect: modules, ports, constants and structural types.
2	
3	The operations here are ordinary :class:`~src.mlir.ir.Operation` subclasses
4	registered against the shared MLIR context, which is what lets the parser in
5	:mod:`src.mlir.parser` read ``inputs/alu.mlir`` and ``inputs/counter.mlir``
6	directly.
7	
8	Every value-producing operation also implements ``evaluate(env)``, the hook the
9	cycle-accurate simulator in :mod:`src.circt.simulator` drives.  ``env`` maps
10	either SSA :class:`~src.mlir.ir.Value` objects (IR mode) or plain signal names
11	(behavioural mode) to integers, so the same operation classes can be used to
12	build a circuit by hand without going through text.
13	"""
14	from __future__ import annotations
15	
16	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
17	from enum import Enum
18	from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple, Union
19	
20	from mlir.ir import (
21	    ArrayAttr,
22	    Attribute,
23	    Block,
24	    Dialect,
25	    FunctionType,

27	    IntegerType,
28	    Location,

31	    Region,

33	    Trait,
34	    Type,
35	    TypeAttr,
36	    Value,

38	)

41	    "HW_DIALECT",
42	    "Direction",
43	    "IntType",
44	    "ArrayType",
45	    "StructType",
46	    "InOutType",
47	    "Port",
48	    "HWOp",
49	    "HWModuleOp",
50	    "HWModuleExternOp",
51	    "InstanceOp",
52	    "OutputOp",
53	    "WireOp",
54	    "ConstantOp",
55	    "ArrayCreateOp",
56	    "ArrayGetOp",
57	    "StructCreateOp",
58	    "StructExtractOp",
59	    "BitcastOp",
60	]

62	HW_DIALECT = Dialect("hw", get_default_context())
63	
64	#: An environment maps SSA values *or* signal names to integers.
65	SignalEnv = Dict[Any, int]
66	
67	
68	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
69	# Types
70	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
71	
72	
73	class Direction(Enum):
74	    """Port direction, spelled as it appears in the textual IR."""
75	
76	    INPUT = "in"
77	    OUTPUT = "out"
78	    INOUT = "inout"
79	
80	    @staticmethod
81	    def parse(text: Union[str, "Direction"]) -> "Direction":
82	        if isinstance(text, Direction):
83	            return text
84	        for candidate in Direction:
85	            if candidate.value == text or candidate.name.lower() == str(text).lower():
86	                return candidate
87	        raise ValueError(f"unknown port direction {text!r}")
88	
89	
90	class IntType(IntegerType):
91	    """``iN`` as spelled by the hardware dialects (always signless)."""
92	
93	    def __init__(self, width: int) -> None:
94	        if width <= 0:
95	            raise ValueError(f"hardware integer width must be positive, got {width}")
96	        super().__init__(width, "signless")
97	
98	    def bit_count(self) -> int:
99	        return self.width
100	
101	    def max_value(self) -> int:
102	        return (1 << self.width) - 1
103	
104	    def mask(self) -> int:
105	        return (1 << self.width) - 1
106	
107	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
108	        return f"i{self.width}"
109	
110	
111	class ArrayType(Type):
112	    """``!hw.array<Nxi8>``."""
113	
114	    def __init__(self, element_type: Type, size: int) -> None:
115	        if size <= 0:
116	            raise ValueError(f"array size must be positive, got {size}")
117	        self.element_type = element_type
118	        self.size = int(size)
119	
120	    def __str__(self) -> str:
121	        return f"!hw.array<{self.size}x{self.element_type}>"
122	
123	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
124	        return str(self)
125	
126	    def bit_count(self) -> int:
127	        return self.size * bit_width_of(self.element_type)
128	
129	    def element_at(self, index: int) -> Type:
130	        if index < 0 or index >= self.size:
131	            raise IndexError(f"array index {index} out of range for size {self.size}")
132	        return self.element_type

135	class StructType(Type):
136	    """``!hw.struct<name: type, ...>``."""
137	
138	    def __init__(self, fields: Optional[Sequence[Tuple[str, Type]]] = None) -> None:
139	        self.fields: List[Tuple[str, Type]] = list(fields or ())
140	
141	    def __str__(self) -> str:
142	        inner = ", ".join(f"{name}: {ftype}" for name, ftype in self.fields)
143	        return f"!hw.struct<{inner}>"
144	
145	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
146	        return str(self)
147	
148	    def bit_count(self) -> int:
149	        return sum(bit_width_of(ftype) for _, ftype in self.fields)
150	
151	    def get_field_type(self, name: str) -> Optional[Type]:
152	        for field_name, ftype in self.fields:
153	            if field_name == name:
154	                return ftype
155	        return None
156	
157	    def field_names(self) -> List[str]:
158	        return [name for name, _ in self.fields]

169	
170	    def __repr__(self) -> str:
171	        return str(self)

174	        return bit_width_of(self.inner_type)

177	def bit_width_of(type: Optional[Type]) -> int:
178	    """Best-effort bit width for any hardware type."""
179	    if type is None:
180	        return 0
181	    for attribute in ("bit_count",):
182	        method = getattr(type, attribute, None)
183	        if callable(method):
184	            return int(method())
185	    width = type.bitwidth()
186	    return int(width) if width else 0

189	HW_DIALECT.register_type_parser("array", lambda body: OpaqueType("hw", "array", body))
190	HW_DIALECT.register_type_parser("struct", lambda body: OpaqueType("hw", "struct", body))
191	HW_DIALECT.register_type_parser("inout", lambda body: OpaqueType("hw", "inout", body))

201	    """One port of a hardware module."""
202	
203	    name: str

236	
237	    Hardware operations can be built two ways:
238	
239	    * from the parser, where operands are real SSA :class:`Value` objects, or
240	    * *behaviourally*, by passing operand **names** as strings.
241	
242	    ``read_operand`` hides the difference so simulators and folders work with
243	    either representation.
244	    """
245	
246	    OPERATION_NAME: Optional[str] = None
247	
248	    #: Set when the operation was built from signal names rather than SSA values.
249	    _symbolic_operands: Optional[List[str]] = None
250	    #: Declared result width (used when there is no result type to read).
251	    _declared_width: int = 0
252	    #: Preferred name for the result, mirroring CIRCT's ``result_name``.
253	    result_name: str = ""
254	
255	    def __init__(
256	        self,
257	        operands: Optional[Sequence[Union[Value, str]]] = None,
258	        result_types: Optional[Sequence[Type]] = None,
259	        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
260	        width: int = 0,
261	        result_name: str = "",
262	        name: Optional[str] = None,
263	        location: Optional[Location] = None,
264	        successors: Optional[Sequence[Block]] = None,
265	        regions: Optional[Sequence[Region]] = None,
266	    ) -> None:
267	        raw = list(operands or ())
268	        symbolic = [item for item in raw if isinstance(item, str)]
269	        values = [item for item in raw if isinstance(item, Value)]
270	        if symbolic and values:
271	            raise ValueError("cannot mix SSA values and signal names in one operation")
272	
273	        types = list(result_types or ())
274	        if not types and width:
275	            types = [IntType(width)] * self.default_num_results()
276	
277	        super().__init__(
278	            name=name or self.operation_name(),
279	            operands=values,
280	            result_types=types,
281	            attributes=attributes,
282	            successors=successors,
283	            regions=regions,
284	            location=location,
285	            result_names=[result_name] if result_name else None,
286	        )
287	        self._symbolic_operands = symbolic or None
288	        self._declared_width = int(width)
289	        self.result_name = result_name
290	
291	    # -- construction helpers ---------------------------------------------
292	    @classmethod
293	    def default_num_results(cls) -> int:
294	        return 1
295	
296	    @classmethod
297	    def build_parsed(cls, **kwargs: Any) -> "Operation":
298	        op = cls.__new__(cls)
299	        Operation.__init__(op, **kwargs)
300	        op._symbolic_operands = None
301	        op._declared_width = 0
302	        results = kwargs.get("result_names") or []
303	        op.result_name = next((r for r in results if r), "")
304	        return op
305	
306	    # -- operand access ---------------------------------------------------
307	    @property
308	    def operands(self) -> List[Any]:
309	        """SSA values, or signal names when built behaviourally."""
310	        if self._symbolic_operands is not None:
311	            return list(self._symbolic_operands)
312	        return Operation.operands.fget(self)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
313	
314	    @property
315	    def ssa_operands(self) -> List[Value]:
316	        return Operation.operands.fget(self)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
317	
318	    @property
319	    def operand_names(self) -> List[str]:
320	        if self._symbolic_operands is not None:
321	            return list(self._symbolic_operands)
322	        return [v.name or f"%{index}" for index, v in enumerate(self.ssa_operands)]
323	
324	    @property
325	    def num_operands(self) -> int:
326	        if self._symbolic_operands is not None:
327	            return len(self._symbolic_operands)
328	        return Operation.num_operands.fget(self)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
329	
330	    def get_operand(self, index: int) -> Any:
331	        operands = self.operands
332	        if index < 0 or index >= len(operands):
333	            raise IndexError(f"operand index {index} out of range")
334	        return operands[index]
335	
336	    def read_operand(self, env: SignalEnv, index: int, default: int = 0) -> int:
337	        """Read operand ``index`` out of ``env``."""
338	        if self._symbolic_operands is not None:
339	            if index >= len(self._symbolic_operands):
340	                return default
341	            key = self._symbolic_operands[index]
342	            return int(env.get(key, default))
343	        values = self.ssa_operands
344	        if index >= len(values):
345	            return default
346	        value = values[index]
347	        if value in env:
348	            return int(env[value])
349	        if value.name is not None and value.name in env:
350	            return int(env[value.name])
351	        return default
352	
353	    def read_operands(self, env: SignalEnv) -> List[int]:
354	        return [self.read_operand(env, i) for i in range(self.num_operands)]
355	
356	    # -- widths -----------------------------------------------------------
357	    @property
358	    def width(self) -> int:
359	        if self.num_results:
360	            return bit_width_of(Operation.results.fget(self)[0].type)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
361	        return self._declared_width
362	
363	    def infer_width(self, type_env: Optional[Dict[str, int]] = None) -> int:
364	        return self.width
365	
366	    def mask(self) -> int:
367	        width = self.width
368	        return (1 << width) - 1 if width > 0 else 0
369	
370	    def truncate(self, value: int) -> int:
371	        mask = self.mask()
372	        return value & mask if mask else int(value)
373	
374	    # -- evaluation -------------------------------------------------------
375	    def evaluate(self, env: Optional[SignalEnv] = None) -> int:
376	        raise NotImplementedError(f"{self.name} does not implement evaluate()")
377	
378	    def fold(self) -> Optional[List[Any]]:
379	        """Constant-fold using the operands' ``hw.constant`` definitions."""
380	        if self._symbolic_operands is not None or not self.num_results:
381	            return None
382	        env: SignalEnv = {}
383	        for value in self.ssa_operands:
384	            defining = value.defining_op
385	            if defining is None or not isinstance(defining, ConstantOp):
386	                return None
387	            env[value] = defining.evaluate()
388	        try:
389	            return [self.evaluate(env)]
390	        except (NotImplementedError, ZeroDivisionError):
391	            return None
392

399	class HWModuleOp(HWOp):
400	    """``hw.module @Name(in %a: i4, out r: i4) { ... }``.
401	
402	    The body is a *graph region*: operations may refer to values defined further
403	    down, which is how ``inputs/counter.mlir`` closes the loop between
404	    ``seq.compreg`` and the ``comb.add`` that feeds it.
405	    """
406	
407	    OPERATION_NAME = "hw.module"
408	    TRAITS = (
409	        Trait.SYMBOL,
410	        Trait.ISOLATED_FROM_ABOVE,
411	        Trait.GRAPH_REGION,
412	        Trait.SINGLE_BLOCK,
413	    )
414	
415	    def __init__(
416	        self,
417	        name: Optional[str] = None,
418	        ports: Optional[Sequence[Port]] = None,
419	        body: Optional[Sequence[Operation]] = None,
420	        attributes: Optional[Dict[str, Attribute]] = None,
421	        location: Optional[Location] = None,
422	    ) -> None:
423	        port_list = list(ports or ())
424	        attrs: Dict[str, Attribute] = dict(attributes or {})
425	        if name:
426	            attrs["sym_name"] = StringAttr(name)
427	        attrs["port_names"] = ArrayAttr([StringAttr(p.name) for p in port_list])
428	        attrs["port_directions"] = ArrayAttr(
429	            [StringAttr(p.direction.value) for p in port_list]
430	        )
431	        attrs["function_type"] = TypeAttr(
432	            FunctionType(
433	                [p.port_type for p in port_list if not p.is_output and p.port_type],
434	                [p.port_type for p in port_list if p.is_output and p.port_type],
435	            )
436	        )
437	        Operation.__init__(
438	            self,
439	            name=self.OPERATION_NAME,
440	            attributes=attrs,
441	            location=location,
442	        )
443	        self._symbolic_operands = None
444	        self._declared_width = 0
445	        self.result_name = ""
446	
447	        region = self.add_region(Region())
448	        block = region.add_block(Block())
449	        for port in port_list:
450	            if not port.is_output:
451	                block.add_argument(port.port_type or IntType(1), port.name)
452	        for op in body or ():
453	            if isinstance(op, Operation):
454	                block.append(op)
455	
456	    @classmethod
457	    def build_parsed(cls, **kwargs: Any) -> "Operation":
458	        op = cls.__new__(cls)
459	        Operation.__init__(op, **kwargs)
460	        op._symbolic_operands = None
461	        op._declared_width = 0
462	        op.result_name = ""
463	        return op
464	
465	    # -- structure --------------------------------------------------------
466	    @property
467	    def module_name(self) -> Optional[str]:
468	        attr = self.attributes.get("sym_name")
469	        return attr.value if attr is not None else None
470	
471	    #: CIRCT spells the symbol ``name``; :class:`Operation` uses that for the
472	    #: op mnemonic, so the module symbol is exposed as ``module_name`` too.
473	    @property
474	    def sym_name(self) -> Optional[str]:
475	        return self.module_name
476	
477	    @property
478	    def block(self) -> Optional[Block]:
479	        if not self.regions or not self.regions[0].blocks:
480	            return None
481	        return self.regions[0].blocks[0]
482	
483	    @property
484	    def body(self) -> List[Operation]:
485	        """The operations in the module body, in textual order."""
486	        block = self.block
487	        return list(block.operations) if block is not None else []
488	
489	    @property
490	    def ports(self) -> List[Port]:
491	        names = self.attributes.get("port_names")
492	        directions = self.attributes.get("port_directions")
493	        ftype = self.attributes.get("function_type")
494	        signature = ftype.value if ftype is not None else None
495	        if not isinstance(names, ArrayAttr) or not isinstance(directions, ArrayAttr):
496	            return []
497	        inputs = list(signature.inputs) if signature is not None else []
498	        outputs = list(signature.results) if signature is not None else []
499	        result: List[Port] = []
500	        in_index = out_index = 0
501	        for name_attr, dir_attr in zip(names, directions):
502	            direction = Direction.parse(dir_attr.value)
503	            if direction is Direction.OUTPUT:
504	                ptype = outputs[out_index] if out_index < len(outputs) else None
505	                out_index += 1
506	            else:
507	                ptype = inputs[in_index] if in_index < len(inputs) else None
508	                in_index += 1
509	            result.append(Port(name_attr.value, ptype, direction))
510	        return result
511	
512	    @property
513	    def input_ports(self) -> List[Port]:
514	        return [p for p in self.ports if p.is_input]
515	
516	    @property
517	    def output_ports(self) -> List[Port]:
518	        return [p for p in self.ports if p.is_output]
519	
520	    @property
521	    def inout_ports(self) -> List[Port]:
522	        return [p for p in self.ports if p.is_inout]
523	
524	    def get_port(self, name: str) -> Optional[Port]:
525	        for port in self.ports:
526	            if port.name == name:
527	                return port
528	        return None
529	
530	    def total_input_bits(self) -> int:
531	        return sum(p.bit_width() for p in self.input_ports)
532	
533	    def total_output_bits(self) -> int:
534	        return sum(p.bit_width() for p in self.output_ports)
535	
536	    @property
537	    def output_op(self) -> Optional[Operation]:
538	        for op in reversed(self.body):
539	            if op.name == "hw.output":
540	                return op
541	        return None
542	
543	    # -- verification -----------------------------------------------------
544	    def verify_signature(self) -> List[str]:
545	        errors: List[str] = []
546	        seen: set = set()
547	        for port in self.ports:
548	            if port.name in seen:
549	                errors.append(f"Duplicate port name: {port.name}")
550	            seen.add(port.name)
551	            if port.bit_width() == 0:
552	                errors.append(f"Port {port.name} has zero width")
553	        output = self.output_op
554	        expected = len(self.output_ports)
555	        if output is not None and output.num_operands != expected:
556	            errors.append(
557	                f"OutputOp has {output.num_operands} operands but module has "
558	                f"{expected} output ports"
559	            )
560	        return errors
561	
562	    def verify_op(self) -> List[str]:
563	        errors = list(self.verify_signature())
564	        if self.module_name is None:
565	            errors.append("'hw.module' requires a 'sym_name' attribute")
566	        return errors

754	    TRAITS = (Trait.PURE,)
755	
756	    def __init__(
757	        self,
758	        elements: Optional[Sequence[Union[Value, str]]] = None,
759	        element_type: Optional[Type] = None,
760	        result_name: str = "",
761	        operands: Optional[Sequence[Union[Value, str]]] = None,
762	        result_types: Optional[Sequence[Type]] = None,
763	        location: Optional[Location] = None,
764	    ) -> None:
765	        ops = list(elements or ()) or list(operands or ())
766	        types = list(result_types or ())
767	        if not types and element_type is not None and ops:
768	            types = [ArrayType(element_type, len(ops))]
769	        super().__init__(
770	            operands=ops,
771	            result_types=types,
772	            result_name=result_name,
773	            location=location,
774	        )

777	    def size(self) -> int:
778	        return self.num_operands
779

781	        if self.element_type is None:
782	            return None
783	        return ArrayType(self.element_type, max(1, self.size()))

786	        """Pack the elements into one integer, element 0 in the low bits."""
787	        env = env or {}
788	        width = bit_width_of(self.element_type) or 1
789	        packed = 0

79	        operations (IR mode).  When ``constants`` is supplied it is used as the

403	    def mask(self) -> int:
404	        return (1 << self.width) - 1 if self.width > 0 else 0

407	        """Push ``value`` in at stage 0 and return what falls out of the end."""
408	        shifted_out = self.stages[-1] if self.stages else 0
409	        self.stages = [int(value) & self.mask()] + self.stages[:-1]
410	        return shifted_out

413	        if stage < 0 or stage >= len(self.stages):

423	    """``seq.fifo`` - a circular-buffer FIFO."""
424	
425	    name: str
426	    width: int = 32
427	    depth: int = 16
428	    clock: str = "clk"
429	    reset: Optional[str] = None
430	    buffer: List[int] = field(default_factory=list)
431	    read_ptr: int = 0
432	    write_ptr: int = 0
433	    count: int = 0
434	
435	    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
436	        if not self.buffer:
437	            self.buffer = [0] * self.depth
438	
439	    def is_full(self) -> bool:
440	        return self.count >= self.depth
441	
442	    def is_empty(self) -> bool:
443	        return self.count == 0
444	
445	    def occupancy(self) -> int:
446	        return self.count
447	
448	    def push(self, value: int) -> bool:
449	        if self.is_full():
450	            return False
451	        self.buffer[self.write_ptr] = int(value) & ((1 << self.width) - 1)
452	        self.write_ptr = (self.write_ptr + 1) % self.depth
453	        self.count += 1
454	        return True
455	
456	    def pop(self) -> Optional[int]:
457	        if self.is_empty():
458	            return None
459	        value = self.buffer[self.read_ptr]
460	        self.read_ptr = (self.read_ptr + 1) % self.depth
461	        self.count -= 1
462	        return value

1	"""Cycle-accurate simulator for ``hw``/``comb``/``seq`` circuits.
2	
3	The simulator walks the IR produced by :mod:`src.mlir.parser`, so the circuits in
4	``inputs/alu.mlir`` and ``inputs/counter.mlir`` are simulated directly from their
5	textual form.
6	
7	Each cycle runs in two phases, which is what makes the result cycle-accurate:
8	
9	1. **Combinational settle** - every ``comb``/``hw`` operation is evaluated in
10	   data-dependency order, treating register outputs and input ports as roots.
11	   Because a hardware body is a graph region, the order is discovered with a
12	   worklist rather than assumed from the textual order.
13	2. **Sequential commit** - every register's next value is computed from the
14	   settled values, and only then are they all written.  Registers therefore all
15	   sample the same pre-edge state, so ``%reg`` feeding ``comb.add`` feeding
16	   ``%reg`` counts by one per cycle instead of racing.
17	"""
18	from __future__ import annotations
19	
20	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
21	from typing import Any, Dict, Iterable, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple, Union
22

24	    Block,
25	    BlockArgument,
26	    ModuleOp,
27	    Operation,
28	    OpResult,
29	    Value,
30	    Trait,
31	)

44	    "SimulationError",
45	    "CycleRecord",

64	    """Every ``hw.module`` reachable from ``root``, in textual order."""
65	    found: List[Operation] = []

77	    modules = list_modules(root)

163	class CircuitSimulator:
164	    """Evaluates an ``hw.module`` cycle by cycle."""
165	
166	    def __init__(
167	        self,
168	        module: Operation,
169	        record_trace: bool = True,
170	    ) -> None:
171	        if module.name not in ("hw.module", "hw.module.extern"):
172	            raise SimulationError(
173	                f"expected an 'hw.module' operation, got '{module.name}'"
174	            )
175	        self.module = module
176	        self.record_trace = record_trace
177	        self.cycle = 0
178	        self.trace = SimulationTrace()

180	        self._block: Optional[Block] = (
181	            module.regions[0].blocks[0]
182	            if module.regions and module.regions[0].blocks
183	            else None
184	        )
185	        self._ports: List[Port] = list(getattr(module, "ports", []) or [])

187	        self._output_ports = [p for p in self._ports if p.is_output]
188	        self._registers: List[Operation] = [
189	            op for op in self._body_ops() if isinstance(op, SeqOp)

191	        self._combinational: List[Operation] = [
192	            op
193	            for op in self._body_ops()
194	            if not isinstance(op, SeqOp) and op.num_results and not op.is_terminator
195	        ]
196	        self._output_op: Optional[Operation] = next(
197	            (op for op in reversed(self._body_ops()) if op.name == "hw.output"), None
198	        )
199	
200	        self.inputs: Dict[str, int] = {p.name: 0 for p in self._input_ports}
201	        self.values: Dict[Any, int] = {}
202	        self.reset_state()
203	
204	    # -- structure --------------------------------------------------------
205	    def _body_ops(self) -> List[Operation]:
206	        if self._block is None:
207	            return []
208	        return list(self._block.operations)
209	
210	    @property
211	    def ports(self) -> List[Port]:
212	        return list(self._ports)
213	
214	    @property
215	    def input_names(self) -> List[str]:
216	        return [p.name for p in self._input_ports]
217	
218	    @property
219	    def output_names(self) -> List[str]:
220	        return [p.name for p in self._output_ports]
221	
222	    @property
223	    def registers(self) -> List[Operation]:
224	        return list(self._registers)
225	
226	    @property
227	    def is_sequential(self) -> bool:
228	        return bool(self._registers)
229	
230	    def register_name(self, register: Operation) -> str:
231	        name = getattr(register, "reg_name", "") or getattr(register, "result_name", "")
232	        if name:
233	            return name
234	        if register.num_results and register.result(0).name:
235	            return register.result(0).name
236	        return f"reg{id(register) & 0xFFFF}"

238	    # -- state ------------------------------------------------------------
239	    def reset_state(self) -> None:
240	        """Assert reset: every register returns to its reset value."""
241	        self.cycle = 0
242	        self.trace = SimulationTrace(self.input_names + self.output_names)
243	        for register in self._registers:
244	            env = self._port_environment()
245	            reset = getattr(register, "reset_state", None)
246	            if callable(reset):

248	                    reset(env)

255	    reset = reset_state
256	
257	    def register_values(self) -> Dict[str, int]:
258	        return {
259	            self.register_name(register): register.get_value()
260	            for register in self._registers
261	        }
262	
263	    # -- inputs -----------------------------------------------------------
264	    def set_input(self, name: str, value: int) -> None:
265	        if name not in self.inputs:
