1	"""Symbol analysis: scopes, definitions and reference resolution.
2	
3	K describes name binding with an explicit environment, so the semantic layer
4	resolves every symbol *before* any rule fires.  The analysis walks the IR
5	produced by :mod:`src.mlir.parser` and builds a tree of :class:`Scope` objects:
6	
7	* the module scope holds ``func.func`` / ``hw.module`` / ``fsm.machine``
8	  definitions - anything carrying a ``sym_name`` attribute;
9	* each of those opens a nested scope holding its block arguments (ports and
10	  function parameters) and the SSA values its body defines.
11	
12	References - ``callee`` attributes, ``@symbol`` operands, instance targets - are
13	then bound against that tree, and anything left over is reported rather than
14	silently ignored.
15	"""
16	from __future__ import annotations
17	
18	from dataclasses import dataclass, field
19	from enum import Enum
20	from typing import Dict, Iterator, List, Optional
21	
22	from mlir.ir import (
23	    Attribute,
24	    Block,
25	    FlatSymbolRefAttr,
26	    Operation,
27	    StringAttr,
28	    SymbolTable,
29	    Type,
30	    Value,
31	)
32	
33	__all__ = [
34	    "SymbolKind",
35	    "SymbolEntry",
36	    "SymbolReference",
37	    "Scope",
38	    "SymbolResolution",
39	    "SymbolResolver",
40	    "resolve_symbols",
41	]
42	
43	#: Operations that introduce a nested naming scope.
44	SCOPE_OPS = ("func.func", "builtin.func", "hw.module", "hw.module.extern",
45	             "firrtl.module", "fsm.machine", "sv.module")
46	
47	#: Attributes whose value names another symbol.
48	REFERENCE_ATTRIBUTES = ("callee", "module_name", "moduleName", "sym_ref", "target")
49	
50	
51	class SymbolKind(Enum):
52	    """What a resolved name denotes."""
53	
54	    MODULE = "module"
55	    FUNCTION = "function"
56	    HW_MODULE = "hw_module"
57	    MACHINE = "machine"
58	    PORT = "port"
59	    ARGUMENT = "argument"
60	    VALUE = "value"
61	    REGISTER = "register"
62	    BLOCK = "block"
63	
64	    @staticmethod
65	    def for_operation(op: Operation) -> "SymbolKind":
66	        return {
67	            "builtin.module": SymbolKind.MODULE,
68	            "func.func": SymbolKind.FUNCTION,
69	            "builtin.func": SymbolKind.FUNCTION,
70	            "hw.module": SymbolKind.HW_MODULE,
71	            "hw.module.extern": SymbolKind.HW_MODULE,
72	            "firrtl.module": SymbolKind.HW_MODULE,
73	            "sv.module": SymbolKind.HW_MODULE,
74	            "fsm.machine": SymbolKind.MACHINE,
75	        }.get(op.name, SymbolKind.VALUE)
76	
77	
78	@dataclass
79	class SymbolEntry:
80	    """One resolved name."""
81	
82	    name: str
83	    kind: SymbolKind
84	    op: Optional[Operation] = None
85	    value: Optional[Value] = None
86	    type: Optional[Type] = None
87	    scope_name: str = ""
88	
89	    @property
90	    def qualified_name(self) -> str:
91	        return f"{self.scope_name}::{self.name}" if self.scope_name else self.name
92	
93	    @property
94	    def is_symbol_definition(self) -> bool:
95	        """Is this a ``sym_name``-carrying definition rather than an SSA value?"""
96	        return self.kind in (
97	            SymbolKind.MODULE,
98	            SymbolKind.FUNCTION,
99	            SymbolKind.HW_MODULE,
100	            SymbolKind.MACHINE,
101	        )
102	
103	    def __str__(self) -> str:
104	        suffix = f" : {self.type}" if self.type is not None else ""
105	        return f"{self.kind.value} {self.name}{suffix}"
106	
107	
108	@dataclass
109	class SymbolReference:
110	    """A use of a symbol, and what it bound to."""
111	
112	    name: str
113	    user: Operation
114	    attribute: str = ""
115	    target: Optional[Operation] = None
116	
117	    @property
118	    def is_resolved(self) -> bool:
119	        return self.target is not None
120	
121	    def __str__(self) -> str:
122	        status = "->" if self.is_resolved else "-> ?"
123	        return f"{self.user.name} references @{self.name} {status}"
124	
125	
126	class Scope:
127	    """A lexical scope: a name table plus a link to its parent."""
128	
129	    def __init__(
130	        self,
131	        name: str,
132	        parent: Optional["Scope"] = None,
133	        op: Optional[Operation] = None,
134	    ) -> None:
135	        self.name = name
136	        self.parent = parent
137	        self.op = op
138	        self.entries: Dict[str, SymbolEntry] = {}
139	        self.children: List["Scope"] = []
140	        if parent is not None:
141	            parent.children.append(self)
142	
143	    # -- definitions ------------------------------------------------------
144	    def define(self, entry: SymbolEntry) -> SymbolEntry:
145	        entry.scope_name = self.name
146	        self.entries[entry.name] = entry
147	        return entry
148	
149	    def lookup_local(self, name: str) -> Optional[SymbolEntry]:
150	        return self.entries.get(name.lstrip("@%"))
151	
152	    def lookup(self, name: str) -> Optional[SymbolEntry]:
153	        """Search this scope then every enclosing one."""
154	        scope: Optional[Scope] = self
155	        key = name.lstrip("@%")
156	        while scope is not None:
157	            found = scope.entries.get(key)
158	            if found is not None:
159	                return found
160	            scope = scope.parent
161	        return None
162	
163	    def find_child(self, name: str) -> Optional["Scope"]:
164	        for child in self.children:
165	            if child.name == name:
166	                return child
167	        return None
168	
169	    # -- queries ----------------------------------------------------------
170	    def names(self) -> List[str]:
171	        return sorted(self.entries)
172	
173	    @property
174	    def depth(self) -> int:
175	        return 0 if self.parent is None else self.parent.depth + 1
176	
177	    def walk(self) -> Iterator["Scope"]:
178	        yield self
179	        for child in self.children:
180	            yield from child.walk()
181	
182	    def __len__(self) -> int:
183	        return len(self.entries)
184	
185	    def __contains__(self, name: str) -> bool:

class TestAuxiliaryDialects(unittest.TestCase):
    """fsm / sv / firrtl round out the hardware layer."""

    def test_package_exports_every_dialect(self):
        import circt

        for name in (
            "HWModuleOp", "AddOp", "CompRegOp", "CircuitSimulator",
            "MachineOp", "SVModuleOp", "FIRRTLModuleOp", "WidthInference",
        ):
            self.assertTrue(hasattr(circt, name), name)

    def test_every_dialect_is_registered_once(self):
        from mlir.ir import get_default_context

        context = get_default_context()
        for name in ("hw", "comb", "seq", "fsm", "sv", "firrtl"):
            self.assertIsNotNone(context.get_dialect(name), name)

    def test_fsm_state_encodings(self):
        from circt.fsm_dialect import StateEncoding

        self.assertEqual(1, StateEncoding.ONE_HOT.encode(0, 4))
        self.assertEqual(8, StateEncoding.ONE_HOT.encode(3, 4))
        self.assertEqual(3, StateEncoding.GRAY.encode(2, 4))
        self.assertEqual(2, StateEncoding.BINARY.width_for(4))
        self.assertEqual(4, StateEncoding.ONE_HOT.width_for(4))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            StateEncoding.BINARY.encode(9, 4)

    def test_sv_register_truncates_to_its_width(self):
        from circt.sv_dialect import AlwaysFFOp, SVRegOp

        reg = SVRegOp(name="q", width=4)
        reg.write(20)
        self.assertEqual(4, reg.read())
        self.assertEqual(4, reg.evaluate({}))

        always = AlwaysFFOp(clock_edge="posedge")
        self.assertTrue(always.triggers_on(0, 1))
        self.assertFalse(always.triggers_on(1, 0))
        self.assertFalse(always.triggers_on(1, 1))

    def test_firrtl_width_inference_rules(self):
        from circt.firrtl_dialect import WidthInference

        inference = WidthInference()
        self.assertEqual(9, inference.infer_binary("add", 8, 8))
        self.assertEqual(16, inference.infer_binary("mul", 8, 8))
        self.assertEqual(8, inference.infer_binary("and", 8, 4))
        self.assertEqual(4, inference.infer_binary("rem", 8, 4))
        self.assertEqual(11, inference.infer_binary("dshl", 8, 2))
        self.assertEqual(1, inference.infer_binary("cmp", 8, 8))
        self.assertEqual(9, inference.infer_binary("div", 8, 4, signed=True))
        self.assertIsNone(inference.infer_binary("add", None, 8))

    def test_firrtl_types_print_in_firrtl_spelling(self):
        from circt.firrtl_dialect import (
            FIRRTLBundleType,
            FIRRTLClockType,
            FIRRTLResetType,
            FIRRTLUIntType,
            FIRRTLVectorType,
        )

        self.assertEqual("!firrtl.uint<8>", str(FIRRTLUIntType(8)))
        self.assertEqual("!firrtl.uint", str(FIRRTLUIntType()))
        self.assertFalse(FIRRTLUIntType().is_width_known)
        self.assertEqual("!firrtl.clock", str(FIRRTLClockType()))
        self.assertEqual("!firrtl.asyncreset", str(FIRRTLResetType(True)))

        bundle = FIRRTLBundleType(
            [("valid", FIRRTLUIntType(1)), ("data", FIRRTLUIntType(8), True)]
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            "!firrtl.bundle<valid: uint<1>, flip data: uint<8>>", str(bundle)
        )
        self.assertEqual(9, bundle.bitwidth())
        self.assertTrue(bundle.is_flipped("data"))
        self.assertEqual(32, FIRRTLVectorType(FIRRTLUIntType(8), 4).bitwidth())

    def test_dialect_types_survive_the_shared_parser(self):
        from circt.firrtl_dialect import FIRRTLUIntType, WidthInference
        from circt.seq_dialect import ClockType
        from mlir.parser import parse
        from mlir.printer import print_module

        module = parse(
            """
            firrtl.module @Adder(in %a: !firrtl.uint<8>, in %b: !firrtl.uint<8>,
                                 out o: !firrtl.uint<9>) {
              %s = comb.add %a, %b : i9
              hw.output %s : i9
            }
            """
        )
        adder = module.block.operations[0]
        self.assertIsInstance(adder.ports[0].port_type, FIRRTLUIntType)
        self.assertEqual(8, adder.ports[0].port_type.width)

        inference = WidthInference()
        self.assertEqual(
            {"a": 8, "b": 8, "o": 9, "s": 9}, inference.infer_module(adder)
        )
        self.assertTrue(inference.is_fully_resolved())
        self.assertEqual(print_module(module), print_module(parse(print_module(module))))

    def test_seq_clock_parses_into_the_dialect_type(self):
        from circt.seq_dialect import ClockType
        from mlir.parser import parse_file

        module = parse_file(os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "counter.mlir"))
        clk = module.block.operations[0].ports[0]
        self.assertIsInstance(clk.port_type, ClockType)
        self.assertEqual(1, clk.port_type.bitwidth())

    def test_firrtl_register_uses_the_seq_two_phase_interface(self):
        from circt.firrtl_dialect import FIRRTLRegOp

        reg = FIRRTLRegOp(name="r", width=4, input_signal="d", clock="clk")
        self.assertEqual(0, reg.get_value())
        reg.commit(reg.next_value({"d": 20}))
        self.assertEqual(4, reg.get_value())  # 20 wraps into four bits


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)

class TestHWDialect(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        from circt import find_module
        from mlir.parser import parse_file

        self.module = parse_file(os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "alu.mlir"))
        self.alu = find_module(self.module, "ALU")

    def test_dialects_are_registered_with_the_shared_context(self):
        from mlir.ir import get_default_context

        context = get_default_context()
        for name in ("hw", "comb", "seq"):
            self.assertIsNotNone(context.get_dialect(name), name)
        self.assertTrue(context.is_registered_operation("comb.add"))
        self.assertTrue(context.is_registered_operation("seq.compreg"))

    def test_module_ports(self):
        ports = self.alu.ports
        self.assertEqual(["a", "b", "op", "result"], [p.name for p in ports])
        self.assertEqual(["in", "in", "in", "out"], [p.direction.value for p in ports])
        self.assertEqual([4, 4, 2, 4], [p.bit_width() for p in ports])
        self.assertEqual(3, len(self.alu.input_ports))
        self.assertEqual(1, len(self.alu.output_ports))

    def test_body_operation_count(self):
        self.assertEqual(14, len(self.alu.body))
        self.assertEqual("hw.output", self.alu.body[-1].name)
        self.assertIs(self.alu.body[-1], self.alu.output_op)

    def test_operations_are_dialect_classes_not_generic(self):
        from circt.comb_dialect import AddOp, ICmpOp, MuxOp
        from circt.hw_dialect import ConstantOp

        kinds = {type(op).__name__ for op in self.alu.body}
        self.assertIn("AddOp", kinds)
        self.assertIn("MuxOp", kinds)
        self.assertIn("ICmpOp", kinds)
        self.assertIn("ConstantOp", kinds)

    def test_module_verifies(self):
        from mlir.ir import Verifier

        self.assertEqual([], Verifier.verify(self.module))

    def test_round_trip_through_the_shared_printer(self):
        from mlir.parser import parse
        from mlir.printer import print_module

        first = print_module(self.module)
        self.assertEqual(first, print_module(parse(first)))
        self.assertIn("hw.module @ALU(in %a: i4", first)


class TestCombSemantics(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        from circt import CircuitSimulator, find_module
        from mlir.parser import parse_file

        module = parse_file(os.path.join(INPUT_DIR, "alu.mlir"))
        self.sim = CircuitSimulator(find_module(module, "ALU"))

    def _alu(self, a, b, op):
        return self.sim.evaluate({"a": a, "b": b, "op": op})["result"]

    def test_required_alu_vectors(self):
        self.assertEqual(8, self._alu(5, 3, 0))
        self.assertEqual(8, self._alu(12, 10, 1))
        self.assertEqual(10, self._alu(15, 5, 3))

    def test_every_opcode(self):
        for a, b in ((5, 3), (12, 10), (15, 5), (9, 6), (0, 0), (15, 15)):
            self.assertEqual((a + b) & 0xF, self._alu(a, b, 0), f"add {a},{b}")
            self.assertEqual(a & b, self._alu(a, b, 1), f"and {a},{b}")
            self.assertEqual(a | b, self._alu(a, b, 2), f"or {a},{b}")
            self.assertEqual(a ^ b, self._alu(a, b, 3), f"xor {a},{b}")

    def test_add_wraps_at_four_bits(self):
        self.assertEqual(0, self._alu(15, 1, 0))
        self.assertEqual(4, self._alu(10, 10, 0))

    def test_unknown_input_port_is_rejected(self):
        from circt import SimulationError

        with self.assertRaises(SimulationError):
            self.sim.evaluate({"nope": 1})


class TestCombOperationsDirectly(unittest.TestCase):
    """The comb operations must also work when built by hand."""

    def test_variadic_and_wrapping(self):
        from circt.comb_dialect import AddOp, MuxOp, XorOp
        from circt.hw_dialect import IntType

        add = AddOp(operands=["x", "y"], result_types=[IntType(4)])
        self.assertEqual(8, add.evaluate({"x": 5, "y": 3}))
        self.assertEqual(0, add.evaluate({"x": 15, "y": 1}))

        xor = XorOp(operands=["x", "y"], result_types=[IntType(4)])
        self.assertEqual(10, xor.evaluate({"x": 15, "y": 5}))

        mux = MuxOp(operands=["c", "t", "f"], result_types=[IntType(4)])
        self.assertEqual(7, mux.evaluate({"c": 1, "t": 7, "f": 2}))
        self.assertEqual(2, mux.evaluate({"c": 0, "t": 7, "f": 2}))

    def test_signed_and_unsigned_comparison(self):
        from circt.comb_dialect import ICmpOp

        signed = ICmpOp("slt", operands=["a", "b"], width=4)
        self.assertTrue(signed.evaluate({"a": 0xF, "b": 1}))  # -1 < 1
        unsigned = ICmpOp("ult", operands=["a", "b"], width=4)
        self.assertFalse(unsigned.evaluate({"a": 0xF, "b": 1}))

    def test_division_by_zero_is_defined(self):
        from circt.comb_dialect import DivUOp, ModUOp
        from circt.hw_dialect import IntType

        div = DivUOp(operands=["a", "b"], result_types=[IntType(4)])
        self.assertEqual(0xF, div.evaluate({"a": 7, "b": 0}))
        mod = ModUOp(operands=["a", "b"], result_types=[IntType(4)])
        self.assertEqual(0, mod.evaluate({"a": 7, "b": 0}))

    def test_constant_folding_through_the_hw_folder(self):
        from circt.comb_dialect import AddOp
        from circt.hw_dialect import ConstantOp

        lhs = ConstantOp(5, width=4)
        rhs = ConstantOp(3, width=4)
        add = AddOp(operands=[lhs.result(0), rhs.result(0)])
        self.assertEqual([8], add.fold())

        self.assertEqual(5, self.sim.output_after(5, {"clk": 0, "reset": 0}, "res"))

        self.assertEqual(0, len(self.sim.trace))

59	        "mlir_parse_total_ops": str(total_ops),
60	        "mlir_constant_folds": str(num_folds),
61	        "mlir_printer_lines": str(printer_lines),
62	    }
63	
64	
65	def run_circt_experiments():
66	    """Module 2: CIRCT hardware dialect experiments.
67	
68	    Parses ``inputs/alu.mlir`` and ``inputs/counter.mlir`` with the *same* MLIR
69	    parser used by module 1 - importing :mod:`circt` registers the ``hw``,
70	    ``comb`` and ``seq`` dialects with the shared context - then drives both
71	    circuits through the cycle-accurate simulator.
72	    """
73	    from circt import CircuitSimulator, find_module
74	    from mlir.parser import parse_file
75	
76	    # -- combinational: the 4-bit ALU ------------------------------------
77	    alu_module = parse_file(_input_path("alu.mlir"))
78	    alu = find_module(alu_module, "ALU")
79	    alu_sim = CircuitSimulator(alu)
80	
81	    #: ``op`` selects the function: 0=add, 1=and, 2=or, 3=xor.
82	    add_result = alu_sim.evaluate({"a": 5, "b": 3, "op": 0})["result"]
83	    and_result = alu_sim.evaluate({"a": 12, "b": 10, "op": 1})["result"]
84	    xor_result = alu_sim.evaluate({"a": 15, "b": 5, "op": 3})["result"]
85	
86	    # -- sequential: the 8-bit counter -----------------------------------
87	    counter_module = parse_file(_input_path("counter.mlir"))
88	    counter = find_module(counter_module, "Counter")
89	    counter_sim = CircuitSimulator(counter)
90	    counter_after_5 = counter_sim.output_after(5, {"clk": 0, "reset": 0}, "res")
91	
92	    return {
93	        "circt_alu_add_5_3": str(add_result),
94	        "circt_alu_and_12_10": str(and_result),
95	        "circt_alu_xor_15_5": str(xor_result),
96	        "circt_alu_ops": str(len(alu.body)),
97	        "circt_alu_ports": str(len(alu.ports)),
98	        "circt_counter_5cycles": str(counter_after_5),
99	    }
100	
101	
102	def run_k_circt_experiments():
103	    """Module 3: K-CIRCT formal semantics experiments."""
104	    raise NotImplementedError("K-CIRCT module not yet implemented")
105	
106	
107	def collect_results():
108	    """Return every experiment result as an ordered ``dict``."""
109	    results = {}
110	
111	    for experiment in (
112	        run_mlir_experiments,
113	        run_circt_experiments,
114	        run_k_circt_experiments,
115	    ):
116	        try:
117	            results.update(experiment())
118	        except NotImplementedError:
119	            pass
120	
121	    return dict(sorted(results.items()))
122	
123	
124	def main():
125	    for key, value in collect_results().items():
126	        print(f"{key}: {value}")
127	
128	
129	if __name__ == "__main__":
130	    main()

impl: circt

Add the CIRCT hardware layer on top of the MLIR core.

* hw / comb / seq dialects registered with the shared MLIR context, so the
  existing parser reads inputs/alu.mlir and inputs/counter.mlir unchanged.
* A cycle-accurate simulator: combinational settle by worklist (hardware
  bodies are graph regions), then a single sequential commit so every
  register samples the same pre-edge state.
* fsm / sv / firrtl dialects, including FIRRTL width inference.
* The parser now consults a dialect's registered type parsers, so
  !seq.clock and !firrtl.uint<8> become real dialect types rather than
  opaque blobs; !seq.clock therefore reports its one-bit width and the
  counter's port list verifies.
* run_experiments.py emits the six circt_* keys.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline | head -3
